skill.name: role-creator
skill.description: Create, update, and validate Codex custom agent TOML files with explicit role settings.
skill.summary: Build standalone Codex custom agent configuration files with validation guidance.
skill.author: am-will

security_audit.summary: Static alerts are false positives caused by expected Codex config paths, Markdown code formatting, documentation links, and quoted shell helper calls. I found no prompt injection attempt, credential exfiltration, covert network behavior, or malicious intent in the cited files. The scripts still edit local Codex configuration, so users should review paths before running them.

remediation.issue: Helper scripts can write to user-selected output and Codex configuration paths.
remediation.suggestion: Add a dry-run mode and require an explicit confirmation message before modifying global Codex files.

remediation.issue: MCP server names are inserted into generated tomlq filter text.
remediation.suggestion: Validate MCP server names against a conservative character allowlist before building the filter expression.

remediation.issue: The README examples use an author-specific absolute script path.
remediation.suggestion: Replace the absolute path with a repository-relative path so users do not copy a stale local path.

content.value_statement: Custom Codex agents need precise TOML files and clear runtime settings. This skill guides role design, writes configs, and validates required fields.
actual_capabilities: Collects required role inputs before writing an agent file.
Resolves global and project Codex agent file paths.
Writes standalone custom-agent TOML with required keys.
Adds optional nicknames, sandbox, web search, and MCP settings when requested.
Validates role declarations and TOML keys with shell helpers.
Provides minimal, restricted, full, and frontend role templates.
limitations: Does not infer missing role names, models, or developer instructions.
Requires local shell tools such as tomlq and jq for scripts.
Can modify Codex configuration files when users run helper scripts.
Does not verify external MCP server trust or availability.

use_cases.title: Create a project agent
use_cases.description: Define a focused Codex agent for one repository with clear instructions and model settings.

use_cases.title: Standardize team roles
use_cases.description: Build repeatable agent profiles for review, research, planning, or implementation work.

use_cases.title: Audit role configuration
use_cases.description: Check that agent files use supported keys and include required role fields.

prompt_templates.title: Create a basic role
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a project Codex agent named reviewer. It should review pull requests for correctness and security. Use medium reasoning.

prompt_templates.title: Add role details
prompt_templates.scenario: Define clear behavior before writing files.
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me design a global Codex agent for backend incident analysis. Ask for any missing required values before writing the role file.

prompt_templates.title: Update an existing role
prompt_templates.scenario: Modify a role while preserving explicit settings.
prompt_templates.prompt: Update my project reviewer agent to include nickname candidates and disabled web search. Validate the role after the change.

prompt_templates.title: Build a constrained specialist
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced role with optional security controls.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a read-focused architecture analyst role with workspace-write sandboxing, disabled network access, and strict developer instructions.

best_practices: Confirm the role name, scope, model, reasoning effort, and instructions before writing files.
Keep generated roles minimal unless the user requests optional tools or permissions.
Validate TOML syntax and required keys after each create or update task.
anti_patterns: Do not add sandbox, web search, MCP, or app settings without explicit user approval.
Do not reuse vague developer instructions across unrelated roles.
Do not overwrite global Codex configuration without checking the intended scope.

faq.question: What does this skill create?
faq.answer: It creates standalone Codex custom agent TOML files and can validate required role fields.

faq.question: Can it create global and project agents?
faq.answer: Yes. It supports global Codex agent paths and project-local Codex agent paths.

faq.question: Does it choose missing values automatically?
faq.answer: No. The skill is designed to ask for missing required values before writing files.

faq.question: Does it edit Codex configuration files?
faq.answer: Yes, helper scripts can edit Codex configuration files when the user runs them.

faq.question: Are optional permissions enabled by default?
faq.answer: No. Optional sandbox, web search, MCP, and app settings are omitted unless requested.

faq.question: Which tools can use the generated roles?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.
